purpose: What data we need to GO AND GET, per asset type, for the wargame to work. A shopping list, not an audit: every field below is something a person can look up in a manual, a datasheet or an ORBAT, with the unit it must be in and the rule that consumes it. Fields we do not need are listed too, so nobody spends a week sourcing gear ratios.

howToRead.blocking: Without this the asset cannot be fielded at all. Collect these first.
howToRead.fidelity: Improves resolution once the asset is playable. Collect these second.
howToRead.derived: We compute it — do NOT go looking for it. Combat Strength, Troop Quality and the counter symbol are ours by design, because they are game abstractions rather than facts about equipment.
howToRead.scenario: Belongs to a scenario (SSI), not to an asset. Ammunition allocations, fire-mission budgets and objectives change per game.

conventions.range: MAX EFFECTIVE range against the stated target type, not maximum ballistic range. If a source gives both, record effective and note the other.
conventions.penetration: mm RHAe at 0 m, 1000 m and 2000 m. Flat figures are expected and correct for shaped charges — do not smooth them.
conventions.armour: mm RHAe frontal, turret and hull separately if available; otherwise a band and a note saying why.
conventions.ammunition: rounds or missiles carried, per weapon, first-line scale only
conventions.perFieldMetadata: Every field needs: value, unit, source (publication or URL), as_of date, confidence (high/medium/low/estimated). A figure with no source is treated as declared, which is a different thing from sourced and is reported differently.
conventions.nulls: An explicit null with a reason beats a plausible guess. 'unavailable' is data; a made-up number is not.

blocking.why: Our key. Stable across refreshes.
The counter label and the FMC entry.
Selects which of the lists below applies.
Force list construction, and flagging when one nation's kit is standing in for another's.
Recce and Fire Support Teams are the precondition for indirect fire; HQs command-activate; logistics enables resupply and rally.
Sets what one counter represents, and drives stacking and mounting.

fidelity.why: Scenario plausibility.
A sighting modifier: a tank is easier to see than a dismounted section.

derived.why: Built from asset_type, role and echelon.
F / W / T follows from asset_type.
foot / soft_skin / armoured_vehicle follows from armour presence.
A game abstraction calibrated by sweep against the rest of the scale. Sourcing it is a category error.
A property of the unit in a scenario, not of the equipment.

armoured.description: Tracked armoured fighting vehicles: MBTs, IFVs, tracked APCs, SPGs, tracked recce.

blocking.typicalSource: manufacturer datasheet, Jane's, national army pages; STANAG level where thickness is classified
blocking.why: Protection band, and the comparison side of every penetration check.
Flank shots are a real column shift; without this a flank attack is worth nothing.
The main armament decides the fire column.
Range bands and the short-range modifier.
Whether a hit can hurt what it hit.

blocking.unit: rounds, split by natures if known (APFSDS / HE / HEAT)
blocking.why: Ammunition is an economy: at zero an FE still fires but at Combat Strength 1.
Mounting and dismounting. An IFV that cannot carry infantry cannot take ground.

fidelity.unit: array of { name, calibre_mm, effective_range_m, type: mg|agl|atgm }
fidelity.why: Coaxial and pintle weapons are the only thing most AFVs can engage infantry with.
Anti-tank missiles use their own fire column regardless of the firer's strength, so they must be recorded separately from the main gun.
Sighting modifier.
How far it can pick a target out. The basis of a recce role.
Hunter-killer: a second sighting attempt.
Only for the exceptionally slow or fast. A per-platform movement modifier against the terrain table.

doNotCollect: engine power, power-to-weight, gear ratios, top road speed, empty mass
hull points, crew size, fuel capacity, range on roads
rate of fire, muzzle velocity, explosive filler mass
why: movement is a table lookup by Move Type and Terrain, casualties are Combat Strength, and no resolver reads any of these

wheeled.description: Wheeled vehicles: IFVs, APCs, protected patrol vehicles, trucks, wheeled recce, wheeled SPGs.

blocking.why: Two unrelated consequences: anti-personnel weapons may engage it, and marsh and water are impassable to it.
Null is a valid and useful answer for a truck.
Many wheeled assets are unarmed; record that explicitly.
The main reason most of these exist.

fidelity.why: Distinguishes a protected patrol vehicle from a load-carrier off-road.

human.description: Dismounted elements — the only assets that can take ground. Sourced from ORBATs and organisation tables rather than equipment datasheets.

blocking.why: A section is about 8, a platoon about 30. The size of the element behind the counter.
What every member carries: rifles, LMG, UGL. Reference human_carried_weapon entries by id rather than restating their figures.
GPMG, light mortar, MANPATS. These are what let infantry hurt vehicles.
Assaults require and spend ammunition; running dry forces a withdrawal.
Dismounted strength is the ONLY strength that counts in an assault. An element that cannot assault cannot take an objective.
Whether it can ride, and therefore whether it can keep up with armour.

fidelity.why: Command activations, morale steadying, initiative and assault modifiers all read it.
HQ, recce and fire support teams can direct mortars and artillery onto targets they can see and the firer cannot.
Breaching, demolition, obstacle-crossing — for engineer tasks later.
A HINT for setting Troop Quality in a scenario. Not the value itself.

doNotCollect: body armour rating, individual load weight, march rate in km/h
why: BGWS has one dismounted protection class, and foot movement is a table row
human.sourcingNote: The current catalogue cannot supply any of this: its 76 'foot' rows are character weapon presets from a simulator, one has a weapon and none has a range. Expect to build this list by hand from ORBATs — a dozen entries covers a battlegroup.

human_carried_weapon.description: A weapon a dismounted element carries. Collected once, referenced by many human assets — this is why it is its own type rather than a column on infantry.

blocking.why: Selects the capability kind.
Anti-personnel weapons may only engage dismounts and soft-skinned vehicles; anti-tank weapons may not engage dismounts at all.
Range band and short-range modifier.
Fire and assault both spend it.
A disposable launcher is gone once fired; a reusable command launch unit is not. This is the difference between one shot and a sustained anti-armour position.

fidelity.unit: { m0, m1000, m2000 } mm RHAe, anti-armour weapons only
fidelity.why: Flat is correct for shaped charges.
A two- or three-man weapon takes people out of the rifle strength of the element carrying it.
True for guided anti-tank missiles: their effect is the weapon's, not the firer's strength.
False for guided anti-tank missiles.
Missile arming distance.
Attacks the thinnest armour; a column shift rather than a penetration change.

doNotCollect: weight, length, muzzle velocity, rate of fire, guidance mode detail
why: none of it reaches a resolver. Crew size is the only weight proxy that matters
minimumViableSet: guided anti-tank missile, reusable launcher (atm, own column)
60mm light mortar (idf, short range, smoke capable)
man-portable air defence (aa) — only if air assets are modelled

air.description: Artillery-equivalent, air and attack-helicopter support, plus uncrewed air systems. These have NO counter on the map: they are fire missions and sensors, so what is needed is the effect and its availability rather than the airframe.

blocking.why: Selects the effect profile.
Calibre and nature set the fire column and whether armour is suppressed.
Everything inside it takes a morale step, INCLUDING friendly elements. This is the field that makes danger-close a real decision.
Someone must see the target: an HQ, recce element or fire support team.
How close to your own troops it may be fired. Smoke is usually exempt.

fidelity.why: Null for air, which has no meaningful range limit on a 10 km sheet; real for tube artillery and mortars.
A modifier rather than a scatter model.
The difference between pre-planned and on-call fires, and a genuine planning lesson.
A UAS is a sensor first.
How long it stays up before it must be relieved.

fidelity.unit: { name, count, effective_range_m, penetration_mm }, attack helicopter only

scenario.why: Rationing is set by the scenario, not by the airframe. This is the resource the plan spends.
Which turns the support is actually available.

doNotCollect: airspeed, ceiling, payload mass, combat radius, airframe dimensions, sortie generation rate
why: there is no air movement and no air combat in this game. An aircraft is a budgeted effect

naval.description: Recommended scope: naval gunfire support and lift only. There are no naval rules, no naval counters and no naval movement, so a hull is either a fires provider or it is scenery.

blocking.why: The only two ways a ship touches this game.
Only to confirm it can reach the sheet at all.
Naval gunfire is rationed like any other mission.

fidelity.unit: array of grid references, amphibious_lift only
fidelity.why: Scenario geography rather than a ship property.

doNotCollect: displacement, hull length, propulsion, torpedoes, anti-air fit, radar fit, crew
why: modelling any of it would be inventing a naval game the rulebook does not have

scenarioLevel.description: Collect these per SCENARIO, not per asset. They are the levers that make two games with the same equipment different.
fields: ammunition allocation, where it differs from first-line scale
fire missions available per support type, per game and per turn
objectives and victory conditions, in grades
starting locations, concealment and dummy counters
weather, visibility and time of day
order verbs and contingency plans per element

acquisitionOrder: 1. human_carried_weapon minimum viable set — eight entries, and nothing infantry-related works without them
2. human elements for one battlegroup on each side — about a dozen entries each, from ORBATs
3. transport_capacity_dismounts for every vehicle already in the catalogue — one integer per row, unlocks mounting
4. armour_side_mm_rhae and atgm blocks for vehicles that have them — makes flanking and anti-tank fire distinct
5. air providers as fire missions, with scenario budgets
6. naval only if a scenario needs gunfire support
